target: Cyprus (CYP), Jordan (JOR), Indonesia (IDN), Japan (JPN), South Korea (KOR), Azerbaijan (AZE), Iraq (IRQ), Tanzania (TZA)
what_was_tried: Searched each; fetched only where a search returned a plausible official page. Tanzania: fetched The Citizen, 'Tanzania affirms gold reserves as strategic assets' (7 February 2025).
result: No institution-level source surfaced. Jordan, Cyprus, Japan and South Korea coverage is all valuation and tonnage reporting. Indonesian coverage concerns the new domestic bullion bank, not BI custody. Azerbaijan's gold sits with SOFAZ, the oil fund, not the central bank. Iraqi coverage says the reserves are 'in America and Europe' with no named holder. The Tanzania article confirms the Bank of Tanzania as holder of the minerals but names no vault or custodian, so it is a holder-without-storage statement, not a custody record.

what_was_tried: 23 WebFetch calls against a cap of about 25, plus 15 searches.
result: Notes to the financial statements remain by far the best page type: 3 of the 4 records came from one Guatemalan note and one Bolivian operations report. Euro-area notes (Croatia, Luxembourg, Montenegro) were uniformly silent, matching the pattern that the disclosing euro-area banks - Portugal, Belgium, Malta-pending - are the exception.
